name: Carol Reed
life: “I still remember my husband counting pension money on a school desk.” Saturday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Carol starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I can put my pension into the joint offer. My husband says choosing the city over our kids needs both our signatures.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and one cuff folded back twice. Carol has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with salt-and-pepper curls. Carol draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first during a conversation.
personality: Carol finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To decide the pension contribution together at home.
family: Jacqueline Ueda is Carol’s younger cousin. Carol chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Jacqueline brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A boat for sale twice*, Jacqueline says, “I put in an offer and withdrew it when my son said he gets seasick every trip.”
connections: Wynn Montoya. A family pension offer and a deliberately low bid test how seriously small investors are taken.
